clue.text: German sex dwarf

blocks.note: G is the standard abbreviation for German
short for rumpy-pumpy, jokey British slang for sex

explanation.surface: A tabloid-style headline about a German man of small stature and his love life.
explanation.walkthrough: Rumpy-pumpy is cheeky British slang for sexual intercourse; here it is clipped to its first half.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the seven little men in Snow White, named for his bad temper.

clue.text: After reflecting, say a card game is rubbish

taken as written

explanation.walkthrough: 'After reflecting' sounds like 'after thinking it over', but it turns the whole string of 'say a card game' back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: Garbage is the American word for household waste, a straight synonym of rubbish.

clue.text: Pressure on wonderful compiler to be front-runner

clue.text: Use envelopes surprisingly prepared in advance

clue.text: German going topless in luxury hotel

explanation.walkthrough: Fritz, a common German name, was British slang for a German soldier; drop its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ritz in London's Piccadilly is the archetypal grand, expensive hotel.

clue.text: Cook tea with me: chicken, perhaps

clue.text: Party with Bill, perhaps, in Venetian offices

explanation.definitionFit: To redact is to prepare text for publication, or black out sensitive parts, both forms of editing.

clue.text: Make quick note about small fish competing for attention?

clue.text: Partying lets pandemic shift

explanation.definitionFit: Displacement is the act of moving something from its position, a movement or change of place.

clue.text: Cockney's announced One Direction singer will make roofing material

indicators.note: announced means spoken out, and a Cockney speaker drops initial aitches

explanation.surface: A Londoner declares that a famous pop star will produce roof tiles.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney is the working-class East London accent, which drops the H, so the pop star's name becomes the tile name.
explanation.definitionFit: Arris tiles are angled tiles laid along the hips or ridges of a pitched roof.

clue.text: Mountain equipment's end went out of shape

blocks.note: ben is a Scottish word for a mountain, as in Ben Nevis
the last letter of the word

explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a past-tense verb phrase, matching the past tense of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that bent was curved or twisted from its original straight form.

clue.text: Drunk oenophile drinking gallons put in specific compartment

explanation.walkthrough: An oenophile is a wine connoisseur; the gallon letter goes inside and the whole lot is rearranged.

clue.text: Break out of revolutionary clean environment at last

indicators.note: a revolution turns something round, so the word comes back to front

blocks.note: pure means clean, uncontaminated
the final letter of the word

clue.text: Excited once more, starts to send texts, which is touching

again means once more
the first letters of the two words

explanation.walkthrough: 'Touching' sounds like emotionally moving but is meant physically.
explanation.definitionFit: Up against means in physical contact with, pressed close to, as a ladder leaning on a wall.

clue.text: Aggression stands out in Trump's ultimate American

explanation.walkthrough: The standing-out word goes inside the two letters for American, after the end of the name.
explanation.definitionFit: Pushiness is forceful, overbearing assertiveness, a mild form of aggressive behaviour.

clue.text: A beautiful region of Wales for cycling; Welshman cycles

indicators.note: cycling moves round in a loop, so the last letter travels to the front

explanation.surface: A Welsh valley recommended for bike rides, where a local man is out on his bicycle.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface places it in Wales, but the answer is a valley in the Yorkshire Dales; the Welsh words are only raw material.

clue.text: Vegetable crisp in a cheesy casing

indicators.note: a casing holds something inside it, so the answer sits within the letters

blocks.note: runs across the words, from the end of the first to the start of the last

explanation.walkthrough: 'Crisp' looks like a snack or an adjective; it is only letters for the run.
explanation.definitionFit: Spinach is a leafy green plant eaten cooked or raw, a common vegetable.

clue.text: Getting hot, takes clothes off to dine at home

explanation.walkthrough: The stripping is literal for the letters: the outer pair are removed.
explanation.definitionFit: To eat in is to have a meal in your own house rather than going out to a restaurant.

clue.text: Give assent to colleague in the style of a knob

definitions.text: in the style of a knob

blocks.note: a nod signals agreement
an ally is a partner or associate

explanation.surface: A nod of agreement to a co-worker, delivered like a pompous idiot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knob' is British slang for a fool, but here it means a lump or node.
explanation.definitionFit: A node is a knob or swelling, so nodally means in the manner of a node.

clue.text: My word is for ever

blocks.note: taken as written
ay (or aye) is an old word meaning always

explanation.surface: A solemn vow: my promise lasts eternally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'My word' sounds like a pledge, but it is the exclamation of surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are old-fashioned British exclamations of surprise or mild indignation, interchangeable in speech.

clue.text: Was informed about a very strange new word meaning 'to the skies'

blocks.note: to have heard is to have been told
taken as written
V is the abbreviation for very
taken as written

explanation.walkthrough: 'Strange new word' reads as one description of a neologism, but 'word' belongs to the link and 'new' is letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Heavenward means towards heaven or the sky, the direction a rocket or a prayer goes.

clue.text: A large diamond for adventurous girl

blocks.note: taken as written
L is the abbreviation for large
ice is slang for diamonds

explanation.surface: A big diamond as a gift for a daring young woman.

explanation.definitionFit: Lewis Carroll's heroine has adventures in Wonderland and through the looking-glass.

clue.text: Domestic slave makes new coats

explanation.walkthrough: 'Coats' looks like garments the slave sews, but it is a verb meaning covers.
explanation.definitionFit: An esne was an Anglo-Saxon labourer or household slave, a word found almost only in crosswords.

clue.text: Novel idea to limit suffering sung in prayer

explanation.definitionFit: The Agnus Dei, Latin for Lamb of God, is a part of the Mass said or sung as a petition.

clue.text: Cheerful judge with rounded figure around waist, essentially

the central letter of the five

clue.text: Affected by woman's short top - until now

taken as written

the opening letter
